# Simulate what COBOL does
data = b'U001U002B007200'
buyer_id = data[0:4].decode('ascii')  # U001
seller_id = data[4:8].decode('ascii')  # U002
book_id = data[8:12].decode('ascii')  # B007
amount_str = data[12:].decode('ascii')  # 200

# When COBOL reads this into PIC 9(10), it will pad with zeros on the left
# or right depending on the implementation. Let's check both:
amount_padded_left = amount_str.zfill(10)  # 0000000200
amount_padded_right = amount_str.ljust(10, '0')  # 2000000000

print(f'Buyer ID: {buyer_id}')
print(f'Seller ID: {seller_id}')
print(f'Book ID: {book_id}')
print(f'Amount string from file: \"{amount_str}\"')
print(f'Padded with zeros on left (standard numeric): \"{amount_padded_left}\"')
print(f'Padded with zeros on right: \"{amount_padded_right}\"')

# INPUT-AMOUNT is PIC 9(10) and WS-AMOUNT is PIC 9(10)V99

"
